title: After
subtitle: After Always · Chapter 28 of 40
content:
The morning after our first kiss, Severus Snape became aggressively professional.

He called me “Consultant” three times before breakfast.

The first was irritating.

The second was funny.

By the third, I understood he was terrified.

“Consultant,” he said, holding out the Ministry file, “you will need this.”

I took it.

“Thank you, Professor.”

His eyes narrowed.

“Not currently.”

“Neither am I a consultant until nine.”

“It is eight forty-seven.”

“Then stop flirting with my job title.”

His mouth opened.

Closed.

I smiled.

“Cruel,” he said.

“You survived.”

He looked away before I could see whether he smiled.

We were leaving for the Ministry at nine thirty.

The castle seemed offensively normal. Students ate porridge. Owls arrived. Someone dropped a goblet. No trumpet announced that Severus Snape had kissed me in a storeroom between nettles and unicorn horn.

I was grateful.

I was also disappointed, which was ridiculous.

Snape ate almost nothing.

I pushed toast toward him.

He pushed it back.

“Not today.”

“You need food.”

“I need not to vomit during testimony.”

“That is a fair point.”

He looked at me as if expecting argument.

“See?” I said. “I can be reasonable.”

“Disturbing.”

Beneath the table, his knee touched mine.

Neither of us moved it.

That tiny contact steadied us more than conversation.

After breakfast, we returned to the dungeon for our coats.

The storeroom door was closed.

I looked at it.

Snape caught me.

“No.”

“What?”

“Whatever expression you are making.”

“I am looking at a door.”

“You are looking at it sentimentally.”

“I didn't know that was possible.”

“With you, apparently anything is.”

I turned toward him.

“Are you regretting it?”

The question removed the humor.

Snape went still.

“No.”

Immediate.

Certain.

Relief warmed me.

“Are you?” he asked.

“No.”

His shoulders lowered by a fraction.

“Good.”

I stepped closer.

“We don't have to decide what it means today.”

He studied me.

“You enjoy postponing definitions.”

“I enjoy not turning one kiss into a legal proceeding before the actual legal proceeding.”

“That is almost sensible.”

“Thank you.”

“I said almost.”

His hand found mine.

I smiled.

“We can do this,” I said.

“The hearing?”

“Yes.”

He looked down at our hands.

“And this?”

My heart stumbled.

“Yes.”

Snape's thumb moved over my knuckles.

“You cannot know that.”

“No. Neither can you.”

His eyes lifted.

“But I want to try.”

A long pause.

“So do I,” he said.

That was enough.

The Ministry atrium was worse than I expected.

Reporters crowded behind a barrier. Cameras flashed. Quills wrote without hands. Snape went rigid the instant we stepped from the Floo.

His hand left mine.

Not rejection.

Protection.

The gesture still hurt.

He saw it.

“Not here,” he murmured.

I nodded.

“Okay.”

His eyes searched my face.

“You understand?”

“Yes.”

The public did not get this yet.

Maybe ever.

It was ours before it became anyone else's story.

A reporter shouted, “Professor Snape, do you expect acquittal?”

Another: “Were you romantically obsessed with Lily Potter?”

Snape stopped.

I felt the temperature drop around him.

The second reporter raised a Quick-Quotes Quill.

“Is it true your Patronus remained hers because you could never love anyone else?”

My stomach twisted.

Not jealousy.

Fury.

They had turned a dead woman and a living man's grief into entertainment.

Snape's face became blank.

He began walking again.

I followed.

The reporter called after us, “Do you think Lily Potter would forgive you?”

Snape faltered.

One step.

Barely.

I moved beside him.

Not touching.

Just there.

He kept walking.

Inside the lift, the doors closed.

The silence was immediate.

Snape stared at the brass numbers above us.

“I hate them,” I said.

His mouth twitched.

“How refreshingly nuanced.”

“I contain multitudes.”

“Apparently.”

The lift descended.

“I wanted to hex him,” I admitted.

“Which one?”

“The one who asked about Lily.”

“That narrows nothing.”

I laughed despite myself.

Then Snape said, “Thank you for not.”

“For your sake or mine?”

“Both.”

The hearing chamber waited below.

Before the doors opened, Snape turned toward me.

His face was pale.

“After,” he said.

I understood.

After the hearing.

After the testimony.

After whatever judgment came.

We would return to this.

To us.

I held his gaze.

“After,” I agreed.

The doors opened.

We stepped out separately.

It did not feel like distance.

It felt like a promise.
